title: Resonance-Seeded Three-Cavity Filter with 500nm Thickness Cap
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses near theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) for cavity layers and quarter-wave values (λ/4n) for mirror sections, with a 500nm upper bound, will concentrate the search in physically meaningful interference regimes and improve best_target_score convergence compared to uniform-random initialization in route_02.
design_principle: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance occurs when optical thickness equals half-wavelength multiples. Seeding optimization near these values reduces unphysical search volume and accelerates convergence to high-transmittance solutions.
proposed_topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 (21 layers total: 3 cavities with alternating Ge/ZnS mirrors)
design_variables: initialization centered on λ/2n for cavities and λ/4n for mirrors
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
improve best_target_score over route_02 baseline of 0.909
manufacturing_considerations: 500nm maximum thickness per layer improves deposition uniformity
Ge/ZnS material pair verified for mid-IR transparency
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot resonance condition: optical thickness = m·λ/2 for constructive interference
Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating λ/4n layers create high-reflectance mirrors
expected_advantages: Reduced risk of unphysical thickness combinations
Better alignment with constructive interference regimes from round 2 onward
known_risks: 500nm cap may restrict optimal solutions if thicker cavities are physically required
Resonance seeding may bias search away from non-obvious optimal configurations
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) materials in a three-cavity Fabry-Perot topology. Initialize cavity layer thicknesses near theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) at 4.45 μm center wavelength, and mirror section thicknesses near quarter-wave values (λ/4n). Enforce hard thickness bounds of 50-500 nm per layer. Seed 40% of initial population with deterministic λ/4n multiples for mirror sections. Optimize for high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands, low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands, at normal incidence in air. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with resonance-centered initialization. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to replace uniform-random initialization with bounded sampling centered on theoretical half-wave resonance values (λ/2n) for cavity layers, enforce 500nm upper thickness limit, and seed 40% of initial population using deterministic λ/4n multiples for mirror sections. This collapses unphysical search volume compared to route_02's broad initialization.
